exact_statement: For q>=1 and 0<p<1, finite FK edge conditionals under any boundary partition lie in [a,p], a=p/(p+q(1-p)). On wired nearest-neighbor boxes [-N,N]^d, the origin-to-boundary probability is at most 2d*p*((2d-1)*p)^(N-1). At d=3,q=3,p=1/10 it tends to zero although all local conditionals are at least 1/28.
assumptions: boundary identifies boundary vertices only in the box example

remaining_gap: No critical-ordering conclusion: the concrete example is subcritical, not p_c.

exact_statement: For q>=1 on Z^d, wired percolation probability theta_w(p) is right continuous on (0,1). A lower bound delta>0 uniform over p in (p_c,p_c+epsilon) implies theta_w(p_c)>=delta.

Choose epsilon with 0<epsilon<1-p_c so the right neighborhood is inside the parameter domain.

exact_statement: On a finite free FK graph with integer q>=3, for S=sum_v(1{color_v=1}-1/q), H_j=sum_C |C|^j and c_j the centered Bernoulli(1/q) cumulants, kappa_4(S)=c_4 E H_4+3 c_2^2 Var(H_2). At q=3 this equals -(2/27)E H_4+(4/27)Var(H_2).

proof_or_counterexample: Conditional mean is zero. Expand E(S^4|FK)=c_4 H_4+3(c_2 H_2)^2 and subtract 3(E S^2)^2. Omitting the variance term is not justified.
